prompt: Put Renata’s three tests in the order the figure asks them.
hint: Repeated, then told, then the role.
items: Has it happened more than once?
Has the person had clear feedback about it?
Does it affect what the role requires?

prompt: A behaviour has happened several times and affects what the role requires, but the manager has only ever hinted at it. What comes next?

choices.text: A performance conversation, since two of the three tests are met
choices.why: All three are needed; without clear feedback the person has never been told plainly.

choices.text: Clear feedback
choices.why: Right: the second test fails, so the next step is clear feedback, not a performance conversation.

choices.text: An improvement plan
choices.why: That is far further down the road, and lesson 20 covers it.

choices.text: Another hint, a little stronger
choices.why: Hints are what failed; clear means specific, said, and written.

prompt: Why does the lesson say waiting too long costs the person most of all?
hint: “This has been a problem for a year.”

choices.text: Their salary is frozen while the manager waits
choices.why: Nothing about salary.

choices.text: They lose the time in which they could have fixed it, and every mild comment told them things were basically fine
choices.why: Right: by the time it is named, the person has lost a year and has every right to ask why nobody said so.

choices.text: Because the manager will be angrier when it finally comes out
choices.why: The cost described is the person’s lost time, not the manager’s mood.

choices.text: The team forgets the examples
choices.why: Forgetting is a risk, but not the cost the lesson names.

prompt: Which of Marcos’s observations did Renata bring to the conversation? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: His empty section in the one-to-one document
choices.why: No: that is information about the meeting, not a performance observation.

choices.text: A page acknowledged and not acted on for forty minutes
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Two weeks stuck on the notification upgrade without saying so
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Two tickets estimated at three days that took over two weeks each
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: What was going on in his life outside work
choices.why: No: she did not know, and it is not hers to raise as evidence.

prompt: What is the one job of the first performance conversation?
hint: What should the person leave knowing?

choices.text: To agree on an improvement plan
choices.why: Renata was nowhere near a plan, and mentioning one would have been a threat.

choices.text: To find out the cause, so that the manager can decide by the end of the meeting what to do
choices.why: She listened for causes, but deciding is lesson 19’s work, after diagnosis.

choices.text: To keep the person motivated
choices.why: Motivation matters, but softening the message for it is how the meeting fails.

choices.text: That there is a concern, what it is, and what happens next
choices.why: Right: everything else is secondary to that knowledge surviving the meeting.

prompt: Why did Renata tell Marcos the day before what the meeting was for?
hint: What would it do to the one-to-ones otherwise?

choices.text: So he would not learn to dread every routine one-to-one
choices.why: Right: a serious conversation sprung inside a routine meeting makes every routine meeting feel dangerous.

choices.text: Company policy requires a day’s notice
choices.why: No policy is mentioned; the reason is the one-to-ones.

choices.text: So he could prepare a defence of each example, with evidence of his own
choices.why: The point is the pattern, and she wanted to avoid arguing each instance.

choices.text: So Sônia could attend
choices.why: Sônia did not attend; Renata told her afterwards.

prompt: Match each way the message gets lost with what it looks like.

pairs.right: ten minutes of small talk and the concern in the last five
“it might be worth thinking about your estimates”
the meeting spent on whether the upgrade was his fault

right_distractors: naming the pattern in the first minute

prompt: Marcos disputes the first example. What did Renata plan to say?
hint: The pattern, not any one example.

choices.text: “I have the dates.”
choices.why: Winning the argument about one example is not the point.

choices.text: “Fine, let’s drop it.”
choices.why: Dropping it erases the purpose of the meeting.

choices.text: “We might see that one differently. What I want us to look at is the three together.”
choices.why: Right: she keeps the conversation on the pattern instead of litigating each case.

choices.text: “Let’s go through the upgrade in detail.”
choices.why: That is the third way the message gets lost.

prompt: Why did Renata avoid the words “performance improvement plan” in the first conversation?
hint: Where was she in the process?

choices.text: Plans are illegal in Brazil
choices.why: They are not; lesson 20 is about writing one honestly.

choices.text: Because only the people team may say those words to an employee, under Caju’s written policy
choices.why: No such rule appears in the lesson.

choices.text: She wanted to keep it vague
choices.why: She was deliberately clear about the concern; she avoided a term that overstated it.

choices.text: She was nowhere near one, and saying it would have been a threat
choices.why: Right: the words would have dominated the conversation and been untrue about where things stood.

prompt: Which of these belongs in the written summary of a performance conversation?

choices.text: “Marcos is unreliable.”
choices.why: A conclusion, not a fact.

choices.text: “Page on 14 April acknowledged at 02:10, first action at 02:50.”
choices.why: Right: dates and times both people can check.

choices.text: “Marcos is going through a family crisis.”
choices.why: He chose not to explain; the summary records only that something outside work is making it hard.

choices.text: “This is a formal warning.”
choices.why: The summary is not a warning, and calling it one changes what the conversation was.

prompt: Why did Renata tell Sônia about the conversation the same day?

choices.text: To hand the case over
choices.why: She did not ask Sônia to do anything; she wanted her to know.

choices.text: Because Sônia needed to read the one-to-one notes in full before the summary went out
choices.why: Renata deliberately shared no more of the notes than was needed.

choices.text: To start a dismissal
choices.why: Nothing had been decided, and the summary was explicitly not a step towards one.

choices.text: Process rules, support for Marcos, and consistency if it became formal
choices.why: Right: the company’s rules, help the manager cannot give, and fair treatment from the start.

prompt: Marcos replies to the summary saying the page was acknowledged at 02:15, not 02:10. What does the lesson say Renata does?

choices.text: Checks the logs and argues if he is wrong
choices.why: The point of the summary is a shared record; five minutes does not change the pattern.

choices.text: Ignores it, since the difference is small
choices.why: Ignoring a correction makes the summary her version rather than a shared one.

choices.text: Forwards the exchange to Sônia, so that the disagreement is on record with the people team
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson escalates a minor correction.

choices.text: Adds the correction
choices.why: Right: the summary invites correction, and a correction is added rather than argued with.

prompt: A manager has mentioned in passing, twice, that an engineer’s code reviews are slow. Now a release has slipped because of it, and the manager wants to “have the performance talk”. What would this lesson say first?
hint: Which test has not been met?

choices.text: Go ahead, since the release slipped
choices.why: The impact makes it urgent, not a performance conversation yet.

choices.text: Wait for the next review cycle
choices.why: Waiting is the commoner failure; clear feedback should come now.

choices.text: Give clear feedback first
choices.why: Right: repeated, and affecting the role, but the second test fails.

choices.text: Bring in the people team to start a plan
choices.why: Far too early: she has not been told plainly what is wrong.
